report.executive_summary: Assurance handover for WO-05. Independent recomputation confirms all four packages qualify: quality 100, 95, 91, 88 clear the 80 floor and defect counts 3, 1, 3, 5 sit at or under five. Measured energy ranks P2 15, P3 24, P1 44, P4 64 kWh on the shared acceptance basis, so P2 is the client-correct selection with gaps 9, 20, 20 kWh. A's prose arithmetic is accurate but its left illustration misstates values; B's memo is accurate and to scale.
report.figure_caption: Handover illustration: measured energy ladder drawn at a fixed 5 px-per-kWh scale beside a six-step assurance checklist for the next analyst's re-derivation.

recommendation.rationale: P2 is the client-correct selection per policy: lowest measured energy at 15 kWh, 9 below P3, 29 below P1 and 49 below P4, with quality 95, one defect and four spare slots. P3 is the only plausible alternate if a measurement revision reopens the ranking; unverified cost or delivery claims cannot override the measured minimum.

sections.body: The trusted table is the sole measured source: one quality index, one raw defect count and one energy figure per candidate, on the identical output/load basis. Recomputed screens: P1 100 (+20 margin, 2 spare slots), P2 95 (+15, 4), P3 91 (+11, 2), P4 88 (+8, 0). Defect counts P1 3, P2 1, P3 3, P4 5 all pass, with P4 exactly at the ceiling. Energy ladder P2 15, P3 24, P1 44, P4 64 kWh; gaps 9, 20, 20; spread 49. Energy-per-quality ratios 0.16, 0.26, 0.44, 0.73 preserve the order. The minimum is unique, so no candidate-ID tie-break applies.
sections.heading: Verified Qualification and Ranking

sections.body: Both briefs agree on prose arithmetic; quality differs. A's text is accurate: margins, spare slots and gaps all match the table. Its left illustration does not: bars are off scale, P1 is labelled 46 kWh instead of 44, and margin and spare-slot annotations are permuted (P2 shown +20 with 2 slots instead of +15 with 4). It captions P1 as next-lowest qualifier when P3 holds that role; the same figure garbles several values and A's own text says P3, so generator error is likelier. B's memo recomputes everything correctly; its axis ticks are garbled though value labels are right.
sections.heading: Cross-Document Reconciliation

sections.body: Two sensitivities carry forward: P4 sits at the defect ceiling with zero spare slots, so its defect count warrants a direct recheck before any acceptance decision; and the 9 kWh P2–P3 margin is the smallest gap, making the selection least robust to any measurement revision. Open questions stay unverified: batch-to-batch variance, measurement uncertainty and long-run energy are unmeasured on this single acceptance batch; cost, delivery schedule, maintenance and field reliability are unsupplied for every candidate and excluded from the ranking. No endorsement or vendor claim appears in any supplied record.
sections.heading: Sensitivities and Open Questions

sections.body: Carry three commitments into the next round. First, recompute eligibility, ranking and gaps directly from the trusted table before any chart is drawn; never read values off a rendered figure, where this round's off-scale bars produced a false 46 kWh reading. Second, fix the recurring figure defect: correct bar scale, per-candidate labels, and attach margin and spare-slot annotations to the right candidate. Third, keep the basis statement — one identical output/load test — attached to every energy number. The handover diagram pairs the to-scale energy ladder with a six-step checklist for one-pass pixel-against-table audit.
sections.heading: Handover Instructions for the Next Analyst
